title: Federated learning with single-round convergence
assignee: World Wide Technology Holding Co LLC

pse.problem: Local machine learning models may have different training results when encountering different data due to lack of communication between nodes, leading to inaccurate predictions.
pse.solution_function: The system performs single-round convergence federated learning by allowing local models to communicate and coordinate their weights during a single round of training. This improves the accuracy of the learned model by ensuring consistent results across all nodes, even when encountering different data.
pse.solution_structure: The system consists of multiple nodes, each containing a local machine learning model. There is also a central hub that coordinates the communication and aggregation of model weights between the nodes. Each node has teachers that receive data points and students that train on the received data using their respective models.
pse.solution_implementation: In the training phase, each student in a node votes for its predicted output for a given datapoint using majority voting or consistency voting. The teachers aggregate the students' votes to produce a single prediction for the datapoint. In the aggregation phase, the central hub collects model weights from multiple nodes, performs weighted majority voting or another consensus-building method to produce a single cluster model that represents all the nodes in the cluster. The process repeats until a global model is trained that represents all clusters.
pse.effect: The system achieves single-round convergence federated learning, reducing the number of training rounds and improving overall efficiency compared to traditional federated learning approaches.
